introH2: 🏖️ What is Chaweng Beach like, and which part should you stay in?
introHtml: Chaweng is the longest and liveliest beach on Koh Samui — a several-kilometre run of white sand and turquoise water with, right behind it, Chaweng Road lined with restaurants, massage shops, the Central Festival mall, and the island's busiest nightlife · But Chaweng isn't one single thing — the middle of the beach is the hub where you step out of your hotel and everything's right there, while the northern end around Bophut and the southern end are much quieter and more private, made for people who came to actually unwind · Another plus of this location is that it sits just 10–15 minutes from Samui Airport, so getting on and off the island is easy · That range means Chaweng has stays from a few hundred baht a night at a beachfront hostel to five-figure luxury resorts and pool villas — and booking the wrong zone can change the whole mood of your trip: you wanted nightlife every night but ended up at the quiet end that needs a taxi, or wanted calm and got a room on the road in the middle of the bar strip · This guide gathers 10 Chaweng Beach hotels we've reviewed in depth, covering every budget — all built from reading real guest reviews, with the good and the honest caveats spelled out, prices compared across 3 booking sites, and direct links to book
mrtHtml: Koh Samui has no rail transit — you'll get around by rental car, rented scooter, private taxi, songthaew (red truck), or hotel transfer; Grab on the island is limited and pricier than in the big cities · Chaweng sits on the island's east coast, just about 10–15 minutes from Samui Airport (USM) — the easiest of the island's main beaches to reach · The zones in this guide: Northern Chaweng / Bophut end — quieter and more private, close to the airport, home to the luxury resorts and boutiques (Centara Reserve, Anantara Lawana, SALA Samui, Amari, La Vida) · Central Chaweng — the liveliest stretch, walkable to the sand, restaurants, bars, and Central Festival (The Library, Chaweng Regent, OZO, Lub d) · Southern Chaweng end — calmer water, fewer people, clearer sea, a short drive into central Chaweng (Samui Resotel) · After dark both ends are far quieter than the middle; if nightlife matters, budget for taxis

entries.storyHtml: Many people still know this place as Centara Grand Beach Resort Samui, a family favourite on Chaweng sand — then Centara gutted and rebuilt it top to bottom and reopened it as Centara Reserve Samui, the flagship of its luxury 'Reserve' collection, in late 2020 · It's a 5-star resort of 184 rooms, suites, and villas on the quieter northern end of Chaweng around Bophut, with a colonial-meets-modern look in warm whites and creams, and a 9.3 score from 1,265 reviews — the highest in this list · Real guest reviews agree on the warm service (staff who remember your name), the breakfast with fresh and made-to-order dishes, the beachfront pool and shady gardens, the Reserve Host who looks after suite and villa guests personally, and a location just ~13 minutes from the airport · Honest caveats from the reviews: it's premium-priced and value is its lowest-scoring category, storage in the standard rooms is a bit tight, and as a large resort it gets busy with families in high season — not a silent boutique · Best for families and couples who want a luxury Chaweng beachfront that's still calm, with high-end service and good food
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If the budget allows and you're a couple, step up to a Reserve Pool Suite or above — you get a private plunge pool and a Reserve Host that clearly change the experience · Families should pick Deluxe Pool Access, where you step straight from the room into the lagoon pool · Book in low season (May–October) for clearly lower rates, and reserve Act 5 and the Cenvaree spa ahead as peak slots fill fast

entries.storyHtml: If you've ever stopped scrolling at a photo of a bright-red swimming pool against white sand and blue sea on Koh Samui, that's The Library — the design boutique on central Chaweng sand that made 'the red pool' almost a synonym for Samui · A Design Hotels member and a MICHELIN Guide listing, the whole hotel plays on the idea of a 'book' — rooms are Pages, villas are Chapters, and there's a real library with an iMac corner — 46 all-white minimalist rooms, suites, and villas in total, scoring 9.0 from 404 reviews · Real guest reviews say the red pool really is as striking as the photos, the rooms are more spacious and cleaner than expected, and the on-the-beach location is a few steps from Chaweng Road's restaurants, massage shops, and bars (location scores 9.5, its highest category) · Honest caveats from the reviews: form leads function here — the all-white rooms show wear in places, the deliberately dim lighting makes reading hard, value is the lowest score (8.5), and the public beach out front is busy · Best for couples, photographers, and design lovers who see a stay as an experience of atmosphere
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Shoot the red pool early when it's empty, or at sunset when the colour is deepest · If room condition matters, ask for a renovated room or villa, or pick a ground-floor Executive Suite that's roomier and comfier · Eat some main meals out on Chaweng Road to keep costs down, as in-hotel prices run higher · And book in low season (May–October) for clearly lower rates
pros: The red pool and all-white design are one of a kind, photogenic from every angle
On central Chaweng sand, walk to restaurants and bars (location 9.5)

entries.storyHtml: If this trip is about the kids and you want a place with all-day things for them to do, Amari Koh Samui is a name families have booked again and again — a 4-star resort in the Amari group (ONYX) of about 190 rooms on the northern end of Chaweng, close enough to the sea and a ~5-minute walk into Chaweng town, but far enough from the bar strip that families sleep well, scoring 8.5 from 1,115 reviews · The heart of it is water and kids — 3 pools, a water park with a slide, and a Kids Club — plus the Amaya Food Gallery breakfast, a market-style open kitchen with many stations that reviewers call more varied than the room price suggests · Honest caveats worth knowing before you book: a road splits the resort, so Thai Village rooms cross the street to reach the sea, the beach out front is shallow at low tide with rocks and seaweed in places, value (8.3) is the lowest category because in-resort food is pricey, and some rooms still await renovation · Best for families with kids and first-time visitors who want a beachfront resort at an approachable price
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: To be truly beachside with the best room condition, specify the Beach Wing and ask for a renovated room when booking · With little ones, request a room near the pools and water park to save on walking · Guests sensitive to noise should ask for a room away from the flight path · And eat breakfast at the resort, then head to Chaweng Road for other meals to keep costs down

entries.storyHtml: If you want to sleep near Chaweng sand without paying resort prices, Lub d Koh Samui Chaweng Beach is the name people mention — a social hostel by the beach with both dorm beds for budget travellers and modern private rooms for those who want their own space · What sets it apart from a typical hostel is 2 pools, a beach bar, and a beach club with all-day activities to meet new people; it opened in 2018, sits about 420 m from the sand and ~12 minutes from the airport, and scores 9.3 from 240 reviews · Real guest reviews say the dorms are cleaner and better designed than most (each bed has a curtain, plug, and reading light), the social vibe makes it easy for solo travellers to meet people, and it walks to Chaweng's restaurants and nightlife · Honest caveats from the reviews: it's a social hostel, so evenings in the common areas and bar are lively and loud, dorm prices run higher than typical island hostels, and the checkout policy is fairly strict · Best for solo travellers and groups of friends who want a fun, clean beachfront hostel that walks to everything
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper and want privacy, pick a Duo room over a dorm bed and ask for one away from the bar and pool · If you're here for the social scene, a dorm bed is better value and easier for meeting people · And in high season (December–February) beds and rooms fill fast, so book ahead and lock in free cancellation

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms outside peak season and can change by date and season — always check live prices and compare 3 sites before booking · The scores and highlights here come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves · Lub d is a hostel — the ฿900 starting price is per dorm bed, while private rooms start around ฿1,700/night · Chaweng is a public beach; cleanliness and buzz vary by zone and season, which is why many stays have a pool · In high season (December–February), long weekends, and Songkran, prices rise and rooms sell out, especially the smaller stays, so book ahead · Koh Samui has no rail transit — get around by rental car, private taxi, songthaew, or hotel transfer; Samui Airport is only 10–15 minutes from Chaweng · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Chaweng Beach hotels, Koh Samui

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best hotel on Chaweng Beach?
faq.a: It depends on your style and budget · For score and luxury, Centara Reserve Samui (9.3), a luxury resort on the north sand, is the top of this list · For a design pool villa on the sand, SALA Samui Chaweng (9.1) with 2 Michelin Keys and the biggest review base · For the iconic red pool, The Library · For families, Amari Koh Samui with 3 pools and a kids' water park · On the lightest budget, Lub d, a beachfront hostel scoring 9.3 from ฿900

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chaweng Beach hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, starting rates run about ฿900–10,000 per night · The lightest is Lub d from ฿900/dorm bed (private rooms around ฿1,700) and OZO from ฿2,500 · The mid range is Samui Resotel ฿3,200, La Vida ฿3,500, Amari ฿3,600, and Chaweng Regent ฿4,200 · The luxury end is SALA Samui and Anantara Lawana from ฿7,500, The Library ฿8,500, and Centara Reserve ฿10,000 · All are approximate starting rates outside peak; in high season (December–February) they rise clearly

faq.q: ❓ Which part of Chaweng should I stay in, and how do the zones differ?
faq.a: Chaweng has three main zones · Central Chaweng is the liveliest, walkable to the sand, restaurants, bars, and Central Festival — best if you want to be out day and night (The Library, Chaweng Regent, OZO, Lub d) · The northern end / Bophut is quieter and more private, close to the airport, with the luxury resorts and boutiques (Centara Reserve, Anantara Lawana, SALA Samui, Amari, La Vida) · The southern end has calmer water, fewer people, and clearer sea but needs a ride into central Chaweng (Samui Resotel) · For calm choose the ends, for easy walking choose the centre

faq.q: ❓ Which Chaweng Beach hotel is best for families?
faq.a: The strongest for families is Amari Koh Samui ฿3,600 — 3 pools, a water park with a slide, a Kids Club, and roomy family rooms, with a walk into Chaweng town · Centara Reserve Samui has Deluxe Pool Access rooms you step straight into the pool from, plus a kids' club · OZO Chaweng has a kids' pool and shallow water at the shore that suits children · For larger families or groups, look at Amari's Two Bedroom Family Suite or the Pool Villas at SALA Samui and Samui Resotel

faq.q: ❓ Is the water at Chaweng clean, and can you swim?
faq.a: Chaweng is the longest white-sand public beach on Koh Samui, good for swimming and strolling · But per real guest reviews, the northern end and parts of the centre get shallow at low tide with rocks or seaweed in places, while the southern end and less-crowded stretches are usually clearer · Many stays have a pool as an alternative, and it's worth checking the tide chart if you plan to swim in the sea daily · Overall the water at Chaweng is still clear and good for swimming — it just varies by zone and tide

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Chaweng hotel, and how do I get around?
faq.a: In high season (December–February), long weekends, and Songkran, book 1–2 months ahead, especially the smaller stays and sea-view/pool-villa rooms that sell out fast; in low season 1–2 weeks is fine and prices drop a lot · Getting around: Koh Samui has its own airport (USM) just 10–15 minutes from Chaweng, and on the island you'll use rental cars, private taxis, songthaews, or hotel transfers · Every platform offers Free Cancellation — lock in a rate that way if plans aren't firm, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
